capture_exclusions: Prospective, suggested, and term-by-term schedules are not degree requirements and are excluded.

ge_college.note: The Cook-Cole source establishes academic ownership. No additional college-wide credit block is published for this program beyond Civitae, the B.S. addition, the major, and university graduation rules.

upper_division.rule: At least 30 upper-level credits must be earned at Longwood. The canonical model contains 18 specifically required or minimum major/Core upper-level credits and reserves 12 upper-level Longwood elective credits to close the published minimum. The international-exchange exception requires advance written college-dean approval and is not selected.

residency.rule: At least 25 percent of the 120-credit degree must be earned at Longwood University. Independently, all 30 upper-level graduation credits must be earned at Longwood, except for the separately approved international-exchange exception.

canonical_path.note: The canonical unit path uses the 3-credit Global Citizenship Pillar route and MATH 250. If either 4-credit route is selected, the published general-elective capacity falls by the same amount.

modeling_notes: The current official program page combines the B.A. and B.S. This composition selects only the ordinary B.S. path and retains the shared 45-credit major.

MATH 171 is a required major course but the catalog expressly counts its three credits in Civitae. It is represented once, in the Quantitative Reasoning Pillar, so the 45-credit major arithmetic remains 30 Computer Science Foundations + 3 MATH 175 + 12 major electives.
The Civitae canonical path is 39 credits: 6 First Year + 18 Pillars + 12 Perspectives + 3 Symposium. The alternative 4-credit Global Citizenship route raises Civitae to 40.
The B.S. addition is MATH 250 (3 credits) or MATH 261 (4 credits). MATH 164 or placement is a prerequisite to MATH 261, not an additional unconditional degree requirement.

The published 31-33 General Electives range is derived from the two independent 3/4-credit choices: 33 credits on the 39-credit Civitae plus 3-credit B.S. path, 32 when one choice adds a credit, and 31 when both do.

The 30-credit upper-level requirement is not an extra degree block. Twelve credits of the already published general-elective capacity are constrained to upper-level Longwood credit on the canonical path after 18 required upper-level credits are counted.

General faculty approval, the graduation application, GPA rules, course-grade rules, Civitae distribution, and programming-language proficiency are retained as zero-unit requirements rather than being omitted from the full degree.

data_quality_flags.message: The evaluator does not yet condition the 31-33 elective capacity on both the 3/4-credit Global Citizenship and B.S. course selections.
The evaluator does not yet enforce when CMSC 210 or CMSC 280 may simultaneously satisfy the zero-unit proficiency requirement and the 12-credit major-elective budget.
Civitae category, SACSCOC distribution, sequencing, and single-count restrictions require course attributes and cross-group evaluators not yet implemented.
